versions.notes:
### 🐛 Fixed

- **The chat no longer freezes when pi asks you something.** A question or a confirmation that arrived while pi was answering could hang the whole window before the question was even shown. It now appears and waits for your answer.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Usage alerts belong to each window.** Every limit (5-hour, weekly, billing period…) now has its own bell beside it. Set an alert on the weekly window without the 5-hour one going off too, and the cards no longer repeat the same alerts block under every model. The alerts you had are copied to each window of their model.
- **Update all no longer spins its cloud.** While PiCode updates, the button shows a progress spinner, and the memory engine restarts once instead of twice.
- **What's New icons stay still.** The step you pick in a demo kept its icon turning; now only progress spinners turn.

### ✨ New

- **🌿 Each session shows its branch.** In the Agent layout, a session that worked on a branch other than the main one shows it on its row, with the lines it added and removed. Point at it to see the branches it went through and, with GitHub connected (Pro), their pull requests.
- **🧬 Work on a session in its own worktree.** Tick **Worktree** under a new chat: the first message creates a copy of your project on its own branch, named after the message, and the session works there without touching your files. From the session's row you can rename it, review its changes, create a pull request, merge it, or open the copy in a window; archiving it offers to remove the copy.
- **⚡ Several chats answer at the same time**, each with its own questions and changed files. When more than one is answering, Tasks lists each by name, what it is doing and its branch.
- **🚀 A shorter first-run setup.** Five steps instead of seven: the agent and its model are chosen together, themes preview beside the grid, and Escape no longer skips the whole setup.
- **📥 Import is cleaner.** It leaves out memory (every pi shares the same one) and whatever PiCode already has, shows each VS Code extension with its store name and icon, and lists only the settings PiCode understands, named as on the Settings page.
- **🔔 Alerts for your plan's limits.** In Usage limits, each model has its own alerts, like alarms on a phone: add as many as you want, each with its own percentage, and switch one off or remove it whenever you like. A mark on the bars shows where each one will go off, and each goes off once per window, inside PiCode and as a system notification when PiCode is in the background.
- **What's New has pages for all of this**, with demos you can play, in 13 languages.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **PiCode starts again when you open a folder that holds the app and is not trusted.** Before, the editor turned off every built-in extension, and the chat, Status and sessions stayed empty.
- **Signing in to Atlassian no longer asks you to trust the site**, and connecting Jira asks for every permission once, so the board no longer asks again. If you connected Jira before, connect it once more.

### ⚡ Faster

- **Status opens at once** with its last reading and updates behind it; it reads git, pi and your plan's usage at the same time.

### ✨ New

- **pi checks your pages on its own.** pi can now use the editor's built-in browser: open a page, read it, click, type and take screenshots, and the screenshots reach the model as images. After changing anything a browser shows, it starts your project if needed, opens the page, tries what it changed and fixes what is off before telling you it is done. Ask it to look at or debug any page, `localhost` included. It follows the editor's own browser setting, not the MCP switch.
- **What's New has a page for it**, with a demo you can play and a button that opens the browser.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **The plan-limits ring follows the model you pick** in the chat box, instead of the one the conversation started with.

Everything new since 2.0.3, in one list.

### ✨ New

- 📊 **Your plan's limits, beside the chat.** A small ring next to the thinking level fills up as you use your ChatGPT, Claude or NaN plan. It turns orange at 80% and red at 95%; point at it to see each limit and when it resets, click it to open Usage limits.
- 🧮 **See where your context goes.** Context in Status shows how full the chat is over the model's window, with a bar and a row for each part: messages, project instructions, pi's own instructions, skills, pi tools, MCP tools and the rest. It says how much fits before the conversation is compacted on its own, and **Compact session** does it now. The Editor layout has it too, first in the PiCode panel.
- 🗂️ **Fold and hide the sections of Status.** Every section except Environment folds with its arrow; right-click any title, the Status tab's menu or the Command Palette to pick which sections you see.
- 📁 **Your projects beside your sessions.** In the Agent layout, the sessions column lists the folders of your workspace. Add one with **+** or by dropping folders, hover one to open a terminal in it, and customise its name, colour and icon.
- 🔌 **Connect any provider in one click.** Providers is a gallery of more than forty services with their logos and a search box. Sign in with ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot and the sign-in finishes by itself, or paste a key. Connected providers show their full name, state and clear buttons.
- 📥 **Import from pi or VS Code, one item at a time.** Pick a source and tick exactly what you want: pi packages, providers, skills, memory and conversations, or VS Code themes, extensions, settings, shortcuts and snippets. Anything you already have in PiCode is kept, and logins only travel if you tick them.
- 📝 **Every changed file, in one list.** When you review all the changes at once, a list of the files sits beside them with the lines added and removed.
- 👁️ **Hide a folder, keep what you need.** Put `!` in front of a path in the hidden files or search settings to keep it visible.
- 🪟 **Sign-in windows in front.** A window opened by a command in the terminal now appears in front of PiCode.
- ⚠️ **Every problem in sight.** Up to 5,000 errors and warnings are underlined in a file, ten times more than before.
- 💬 **Conversations whose folder is gone ask first.** You can continue in the open folder or copy the conversation into it.
- 🎬 **What's New** has a page to try each of these, and shows only the pages of the version you run.

### 🐛 Fixed

- 🔄 **Updates install when PiCode restarts.** The new version was downloaded but the switch could be skipped because a helper kept your profile busy. PiCode now closes it first, and the installer waits for your profile to be free.
- 🧠 **The memory engine closes with PiCode.** It could stay running on its own, keeping files busy and blocking updates. Now it always stops when PiCode quits.
- 💰 **The cost in Status counts the cache warm-ups**, so the total is no longer too low.
- 🧹 **Status is tidier.** The cards line up in rows, the Updates card no longer shows up empty, and every colour follows your theme.
- 🌐 **The update notice speaks your language.**

### 🧩 Under the hood

- The editor is now based on VS Code 1.146.
- pi 1.5.2, gentle-pi 4.8.0, gentle-engram 0.8.0 and the memory engine 3.7.2. Your memory is not migrated.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **What's New now speaks your language.** The list of fixes is translated into all 13 languages, and the window keeps the news of the 2.0 line together with every fix since, so nothing disappears when you update between fixes.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **The What's New window lists fixes under "Bugs fixed".** When an update only brings fixes, the window still opens and shows them in their own page, and it no longer appears blank when a version has no pages of its own.
- **Updating no longer stops at "Access denied".** The memory engine that PiCode carries is now closed right before the update replaces its folder, so it can no longer keep files open. An engine installed by another program is left alone.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Connecting Jira no longer depends on your browser.** Some browsers never opened PiCode again after you agreed on Atlassian's page, so the connection never finished. Now a PiCode page shows which account gets the connection, you confirm it there, and the editor notices by itself.

### ⭐ PiCode Pro

- **GitHub and Jira issues in the editor.** See what was reported on the project you have open, right beside your code. Each folder shows its own repository or Jira space.
- **A real Jira board.** The same columns as in Jira: drag cards between them, or open an issue to change its type, priority, people, labels or description. GitHub issues can be edited too.
- **Fix with pi.** One button writes the issue into a new chat for you to review. Nothing is sent until you say so, and a report from outside your team is marked as such.
- **An Account window.** Your plan, cloud sync, connections and Pro features in one place. Choose what syncs, part by part.
- **Your connections are safer.** GitHub and Jira access now stays encrypted on our servers, not on your computer.
- **Buying or cancelling Pro shows up by itself.** PiCode notices the change when you come back to the window, with no need to sign in again.

### ✨ New for everyone

- **What's New you can try.** A window explains each novelty, says if it is free or Pro, and lets you play with a small demo or press the button that does the real thing.
- **A new About window.** Check for updates and get them from there, copy any detail with a click, and find what is hidden behind the mascot.
- **See what the agent is doing.** On longer jobs, Status and Tasks show the plan, how far along it is and what is happening right now.
- **Background jobs in view.** Long commands the agent leaves running appear in Tasks with their output, move to Finished by themselves, and the agent's reply reaches your chat even after its turn was over.
- **Memory filters.** Filter your memories by type, scope and date, and search finds more results per project.
- **A better empty chat.** New chats suggest where to start.

### 🔒 Security

- **Opening a folder no longer runs its code without your permission.** A project's own extensions, packages, settings and MCP servers only load once you trust the folder.
- **Safer sign-in.** A web page can no longer sign the editor in to someone else's account.
- **Signed updates.** PiCode checks that an update notice really comes from PiCode, and ignores it if it doesn't.

### ⚡ Faster

- **Issues don't reload** when you switch between panels: the last list appears at once.
- **A quieter Status column.** It checks for changes less often and doesn't redraw when nothing changed.
- **Lighter background work,** and the session list appears sooner after starting.

### 🐛 Fixed and tidied

- **Going back to the Editor layout** no longer leaves the bottom panel open.
- **The Agent layout always opens on Status,** without an empty gap at the top of it.
- **Updating the memory engine now takes effect:** PiCode offers to restart it, with no need to close every window.
- **Undo these changes** asks first, and says so if they were already undone.
- **Changes** in Status opens and closes its list with the same click, and **Tasks** lists only agents and tasks working for you.
- **The chat's Ask / Allow all picker is gone.** It promised a choice that did not exist: the agent runs its tools without asking. MCP servers connected in the editor keep asking.
- **Show Release Notes is gone** from the Help menu: Show What's New tells you what changed.

### ✨ New

- **Two ways of working: Agent or Editor.** Editor is the VS Code you know. Agent puts the chat in the middle, your sessions on the left and a review bar on the right. Switch any time with the robot button, no restart. In Agent the chat has no extra tab row above it, the sessions column reaches the bottom of the window, and the "Pi" picker under the message box is gone.
- **A Status column next to the chat.** Where the agent works, how full the conversation is, your MCP servers, the lines you changed (one click reviews every change), its tasks and what your memory holds.
- **13 languages.** The editor, the setup and everything PiCode adds are translated. The setup opens in your computer's language and gets it ready for the editor.
- **A new first-run setup.** Pick how you work, sign in or sign up from your account card, and change language with each country's flag. The page keeps its place when you choose something.
- **Voice dictation in the chat.** Talk and your words are typed phrase by phrase, all on your own computer. The microphone ring follows your voice and the message can send itself after a pause. It downloads only when you ask, with progress, and can be cancelled.
- **What's New after every update.** A window tells you what changed, including every version you skipped, in one list. It is also in the Help menu (Show What's New), and if you are still on the Editor layout it offers a button to try Agent. PiCode no longer sends you to the repository's release page after an update.
- **Thinking level as a dropdown.** Pick how hard the AI thinks from a small list under its button, like the model picker.
- **Reasoning and command cards, tidied.** The AI's reasoning reads calmer, and an opened command card shows the command that ran and what it printed.
- **Easier code sign-in.** When signing in with a code, PiCode copies the code and opens the page for you.
- **Clearer cost.** In Status, a "~" before the cost means it is an estimate, not what your provider charged.
- **What's new in your packages.** After updating a package that lists its changes, a "What's new" button shows them.
- **White logos on dark themes.** GitHub and similar dark logos are readable again.

### 🐛 Fixed

- Updating the portable version no longer opens empty command windows.
- A finished tool call's command box is no longer empty.
- On the MCP servers page, "Needs sign-in" no longer hides behind the sign-in button.

### 🔧 Other changes

- The built-in AI agent (pi) is updated to 1.5, with safer sign-ins and better stability on Windows.
- Engram, the memory pi uses, is updated to 3.6.

### ✨ New

- cleaner Status, Gentle AI, MCP, Packages and Memory panels
